chapter: Theaters, the Navy and the Singletons' partnership
title: Chauffeuring after the Navy; his mother the cook and Tuskegee
summary: After the Navy Zutty drove a Cadillac for a family. His mother cooked for Madame Le Jeune, who wanted him to finish school so she could send him to Tuskegee.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well when you came out of the Navy then what happens now?
Then I started driving an automobile, for (Dr. Coca?).
Why did you do that?
That's what I wanted to do.
(LAUGHTER).
I didn't know anything else.
Well I mean was that the matter of a uniform again?
No, no uniform. I just wore

my cap. Yes I worked for (Bryant) and they had a big Cadillac and the kids, oh they loved me, you see. And my mother was really a professional cook. She was a chef you see, because I remember when we used to go, they called her Madame (Hendon Le Jeune).
How do you spell that? Hendon?
Yes.
What does that mean?
It's a big building in New Orleans by the name of the Hendon Building.
Oh, I see.

Looked like that was the name of her husband. Then I knew all the kids. The son's kids see, and she was sort of a, she was a grandmother. Madame Le Jeune. And she was always after me to go to school and finish up in New Orleans so she could send me to (Tuskegee). That's what she wanted because she thought that Booker T. Washington was the greatest educator in the world at that time, you know. And that's what she wanted me to do for mama, you know. She says, I just hope Zutty stay in school so I can send him to (Tuskegee) that's where I want him to go.
Well that was the right idea.
It sure was.
Yes, it was.
But maybe I wouldn't have got the other things.
Well that's right.
You see.
That's right, yes.
